nodes.title: Simultaneous algebraic pole clearing
nodes.statement: Let L have coefficients in ℚ̄(x), let α be an algebraic singular point with the meromorphic-basis condition, and let p∈ℚ̄(x) be nonconstant and regular at α. There is a nonzero q∈ℚ̄[t] such that q(p(x)) times every local solution is holomorphic at α. One can clear finitely many such singularities simultaneously. A nonzero rational polynomial also suffices for any finite set of algebraic images: use sufficiently high powers of their minimal polynomials, thereby adjoining the finite conjugate closure; the original image set need not be Galois-saturated.
proofSteps: Choose the maximum pole order from the meromorphic basis.
Use a sufficiently high power of t−p(α); its composition has positive vanishing order because p is nonconstant.
Multiply the finitely many required factors; impose conjugate saturation only when rational coefficients are requested.

For rational coefficients, replace each linear image factor by its rational minimal polynomial and raise it to a sufficiently high power; characteristic zero makes each algebraic root simple, and extra conjugate roots cause no difficulty.
acceptance: For h=x⁻¹ at α=0 and p=x², q=t clears the pole.
No nonzero polynomial clears e^(1/x).
For the unsaturated singleton image √2, q(t)=(t²−2)^m has rational coefficients and a zero of order m at √2, so sufficiently large m clears any finite pole order.

nodes.title: Hempel’s accessory-parameter formula
nodes.statement: Let S={p₀,…,p_N}⊂ℂ consist of distinct finite points, |S|≥3; thus infinity is unpunctured in ℙ¹∖S. nodes.title: Removing zeros with a finite Blaschke product
nodes.statement: Let g be holomorphic near the closed unit disc and not identically zero. Form B from all its zeros in the closed disc with their orders. proofSteps: Let α be the measure of {H≥1}; apply concavity of log with its normalized restricted measure.
Use −αlog α≤1/e and split whether ∫H is at most or above one.
acceptance: For H=0 the left side is zero under the positive-log convention.

nodes.title: The zero-free logarithmic derivative estimate
nodes.statement: For g holomorphic and zero-free near the closed radius-R disc, g(0)=1 and 0<r<R, m(r,g′/g)≤log⁺((m(R,g)/r)·R/(R−r))+log 2+1/e. Use ≤ in the reusable signature; the source states the corresponding strict bound.
proofSteps: Apply the derivative Herglotz formula, integrate its inverse-square kernel exactly and obtain ∫|g′/g|≤4Rm(R,g)/(R²−r²).
Use the L1 identity and Fubini to bound the mean controlling log⁺.
Apply the entropy estimate and simplify constants.
acceptance: For g=e^z the left side is zero; for g=1 it is also zero.

nodes.title: Uniform transfer from small radii
nodes.statement: For 0<r<1 put ρ=max(r,1/4) and R=(1+r)/2. Then ρ≥1/4, ρ<R and R−ρ≥(1−r)/4. If h is holomorphic on 𝔻, m(r,h)≤m(ρ,h), allowing the log-derivative bound at ρ to remove its 1/r factor uniformly.
proofSteps: Check the inequalities separately for r≥1/4 and r<1/4.
Apply monotonicity to the holomorphic derivative ratios used below.

nodes.title: The logarithmic derivative of the omitted-value function
nodes.statement: Let f=1−F_N^N, N≥2, and 0<r<1. Set R=(1+r)/2 and L_N(r)=log(max(1,sup_(|z|=R)log⁺|F_N(z)|)). Then m(r,f′/f)≤C(log(N/(1−r))+L_N(r)) for an absolute effective C. f is zero-free and f(0)=1.
proofSteps: Apply the normalized derivative bound at ρ to f.
Bound m(R,f) by N sup log⁺|F_N|+log 2 and take the positive logarithm.
Use the transfer inequalities to absorb the 1/ρ and R/(R−ρ) factors uniformly.
acceptance: The auxiliary nonnegative L_N is a precise totalized version of the source double-log supremum.

nodes.title: The covering derivative reciprocal bound
nodes.statement: For N≥2 and 0<r<1, m(r,F_N/F_N′)≤T_D(r,F_N)+C(log(N/(1−r))+L_N(r)), where the outer radius in L_N is (1+r)/2. The ratio is holomorphic since F_N′ never vanishes.

Use local inversion for F_N′/F_N, whose trailing coefficient is one, and the étale identity for its pole count.
Combine m(1/F_N)+N_D(1/F_N)=T_D(F_N)−log γ_N≤T_D(F_N), using γ_N>1 from its positive log series.
